method: Tested the actual public https://watersandco.info/enquire endpoint directly via curl (not just the local hub) to reproduce the exact 500 the Owner's tester saw, then traced the chain (Funnel proxy target vs actual bind address) with ss/curl at each hop rather than guessing.
root_cause_ownership: The (1) cause was my own error from an earlier ad-hoc restart that didn't preserve production env vars. Owning it plainly rather than only fixing forward.
lesson: When restarting a long-running production process, always use its own documented launcher (launch_hub.sh), never an ad-hoc command in a bare shell -- env vars that were only ever manually exported are invisible and get silently lost.

Loss figures (55+ reported >$53M in 2025; remote-access scams ~$17,943/victim) came from secondary press/industry summaries of ACCC/NASC data, NOT the primary report, and were flagged as such in both drafted docs.

lesson: A high total score does not by itself mean 'new business line'. When the deliverable is already supplied free by well-funded bodies AND already bundled into the paid incumbent's existing session, the correct product decision is to NAME the work as a reason to book what is already sold, not to price it as a separate thing. Same call as the Concession re-classification. Second lesson, specific to seniors: refuse to fear-price -- a premium charged against a $0 government alternative invites the family to find the free option and read the paid one as opportunistic. Third: when a service's own shape resembles the fraud it prevents, the anti-scam boundaries (booked by the adult child, never cold-called, never credential custody, never operate the account) are part of the product design, not boilerplate.

context: Daily opportunity scan, 2026-08-13. Candidate: chase a sole-trader tradie's overdue invoices for them. On paper the strongest reuse candidate of the day -- same trades base as GBP/ReviewGen/MissedCall, same shape as Bookkeeping and Job-Software Activation, and chasing money is the textbook 'can't be bothered doing it themselves' job.
decision: Scored 25/35 but REJECTED regardless, on criterion #1 = 0. WA's Debt Collectors Licensing Act 1964 requires a licence for anyone who, on behalf of another person, collects or requests payment of debts. Do not revisit without a licence.
method: Verified against the regulator, not memory. Consumer Protection WA (fetched): licence required to 'do any debt collecting tasks'; exemptions are legal practitioners, public accountants, sheriffs/bailiffs, liquidators, banks/friendly societies, trustees -- a bookkeeper is not a public accountant, so the existing Bookkeeping line carries no exemption across. Unlicensed operation risks a fine up to $50,000 AND no entitlement to be paid for the work. ABLIS (fetched) gave the hard numbers: $2,630 application for a 3-year licence, $6,000 fidelity bond (individual) / $10,000 (company), $2,630 renewal, minimum age 21, fit-and-proper assessment by the Commissioner for Police. Honest limit recorded: the exact text of s.4 could not be read (AustLII returned HTTP 403), so this rests on the regulator's plain-language statement plus ABLIS; Licensing Services 1300 304 064 would settle edge cases.
outcome: Logged as a documented reject in candidates_log.md alongside Declutter-to-Cash. Compliant residual identified and requires nothing new: configure the client's own Xero/ServiceM8/Tradify so THE CLIENT'S OWN BUSINESS sends automated pre-due and overdue reminders -- Waters & Co never requests payment on behalf of another. That is the existing Job-Software Activation / Bookkeeping scope, unchanged.
lesson: The second time in four days that the highest-reuse-looking candidate turned out to be a state-licensed activity (Declutter-to-Cash / second-hand dealer, now invoice chasing / debt collector). Pattern worth carrying: any service where Waters & Co would act ON BEHALF OF a client toward a third party for money -- selling their goods, collecting their debts, placing them with a provider -- should be licence-checked with the WA regulator BEFORE any scoring work, because criterion #1 zeroes it regardless of how good the rest of the score looks. Also: 'not entitled to be paid for the work' is a sharper killer than the fine, and is easy to miss if only the penalty is read.
